steps.title: Bright and savoury
steps.body: Sangiovese gives medium-bodied reds with sour cherry, red plum, tomato leaf, dried herbs and, with age, leather and earth. Acidity is high, tannins firm and often slightly drying, like strong tea. Colour is medium ruby, fading early to garnet. It's Italy's most planted grape.
steps.highlight: Sour cherry, high acidity, tea-like tannin

steps.title: Blood of Jupiter
steps.body: Sangiovese may come from sanguis Jovis, Latin for the blood of Jupiter. DNA shows it's a cross of Ciliegiolo and Calabrese di Montenuovo, linking Tuscany and the south. It's genetically unstable, with many clones: Sangiovese Grosso, with bigger berries, is used in Montalcino, where it's called Brunello.

steps.prompt: What does Sangiovese's name possibly mean?
steps.explanation: Sanguis Jovis, Latin for the blood of Jupiter.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for medium ruby or garnet colour, often with an orange tint even when quite young. On the nose, sour cherry, herbs and earth. On the palate, high acidity and grainy, drying tannin. That combination of sour cherry and tea-like tannin, plus the urge to eat something with tomato, is the clue.

steps.prompt: Sangiovese is usually deeply coloured and low in acidity.
steps.explanation: Not true. It's medium in colour and high in acidity.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sangiovese gives sour cherry, herbs and earth
It has high acidity and firm, tea-like tannin
It's Italy's most planted grape, with many clones
